sources.role: official manual for paths, input, saves, states and command line
official Windows download and supported-platform statement

paths.path: bgb.ini beside bgb.exe by default; -ini <filename> selects a different INI.
bgb.ini settings written by Options > Joypad > configure keyboard/configure game controller; controller IDs 1-16 are legacy JoyGetPosEx and 17-20 are XInput, while extra-button hotkeys are mappable.
paths.naming: The official manual documents the GUI and numeric controller-ID semantics, not a stable portable controller-profile grammar; preserve bgb.ini rather than inventing keys.
evidence: docs:bgb.bircd.org manual lines 142-147 (joypad wizard and IDs)

paths.path: <ROM directory>\<ROM basename>.sav by default; the Misc Save files setting can redirect all battery files to a directory; -loadbatt selects an explicit file.
paths.naming: <ROM basename>.sav raw battery RAM; MBC3 RTC data may append 48 bytes in VBA-compatible mode.
evidence: docs:bgb.bircd.org manual SAV format and Misc options

paths.path: User-selected save-state path from the state dialog; -stateonexit <filename> and -state <filename> provide explicit paths.
paths.naming: State filename is user-selected (official example game.sna); current format is versioned and old 0.x states are not interchangeable with BGB 1.0+.
evidence: docs:bgb.bircd.org manual save/load state and command line

paths.path: No BIOS is required for ordinary GB/GBC emulation. Optional DMG/CGB/SGB boot ROMs are selected from BGB's settings and may be supplied as user files.
paths.naming: Boot ROM filenames are user-selected; BGB's official manual does not publish canonical checksums for these optional ROMs.
evidence: docs:bgb.bircd.org manual bootrom settings and speedrun bootrom notes

paths.path: No external decryption/key file is used by BGB.
paths.naming: No external key filename or canonical key checksum.
evidence: docs:bgb.bircd.org manual (ROM, battery and optional boot ROM only)

linux.reason: BGB officially distributes a Windows executable; Wine operation is documented, but there is no native Linux package whose paths can be captured as a separate runtime.
evidence: docs:bgb.bircd.org manual supported platforms (Windows and Wine)

linux-flatpak.reason: No official BGB Flatpak package is documented.

macos.reason: The official BGB distribution is a Windows executable; the manual mentions Wine on OS X but no native macOS package.
